examples.en: In a school zone, you must slow down.
I can see a sign over there saying it is a slow-down zone.

examples.ko: 눈길에서 급한 감속은 오히려 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: On a snowy road, sudden slowing down can actually be dangerous.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 감속 운전이 안전해요.
examples.en: On rainy days, driving at a reduced speed is safer.

examples.ko: 감속을 하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you do not slow down, an accident can happen.
The car behind was startled by the sudden slowing down.

explain: 속도를 줄이는 일을 뜻하고 반의어는 '가속'이에요. 도로 표지판, 교통 안내, 운전 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 평소 말로는 '속도를 줄이다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Cars have to slow down on a curve.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감속'에 '하다'를 붙여 속도를 줄이는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds 하다 to 감속 to describe the action of reducing speed.

phrases.example: 학교 앞은 감속 구간이라서 천천히 가야 해요.
phrases.en: The area in front of the school is a slow-down zone, so you must go slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도로 표지판에 나오는 말로, 속도를 줄여야 하는 길을 뜻해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A road-sign term for a stretch where you must reduce speed.

phrases.en: It's raining, so please drive more slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소 말로 '감속'과 같은 뜻을 쉽게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday way to say the same thing as 감속.

explain_en: It means reducing speed, and its opposite is '가속'. It appears on road signs, in traffic notices and in driving talk. In everyday speech people say '속도를 줄이다'.

examples.en: The miners went into the deep tunnel.
The tunnel suddenly collapsed, so a rescue team was dispatched.

examples.ko: 좁은 갱도를 따라 한참 걸어가야 해요.
examples.en: You have to walk along the narrow tunnel for a long time.

examples.ko: 옛 탄광 갱도는 지금 관광지가 되었어요.
examples.en: The tunnels of the old coal mine have now become a tourist spot.
Inside the tunnel it is dark and the air feels stuffy.

examples.ko: 갱도 입구에 안전 표지판이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: A safety sign is posted at the tunnel entrance.

explain: 광산이나 탄광 사고 뉴스에서 자주 들리는 말이에요. 길게 파 놓은 통로라서 '터널'과 비슷하지만, 갱도는 광산 안의 길에만 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '탄광 안'이라고 말하는 사람도 많아요.

phrases.en: The miners were trapped in the mine shaft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광산 사고 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common usage in mine accident news.
phrases.en_equiv: to be trapped in a shaft

phrases.en: The miners dug a long tunnel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광산에서 땅속 길을 만드는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for making underground passages in a mine.

phrases.en: They do a safety check at the entrance of the shaft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광산 안으로 들어가는 문 같은 곳을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Points to the doorway into the mine.

explain_en: You often hear it in news about mine accidents. It is similar to '터널' (tunnel), but 갱도 is used only for passages inside a mine. In daily talk many people just say '탄광 안' (inside the coal mine).

en: to go via; to stop over

examples.ko: 이 버스는 시청을 경유해서 공항에 가요.
examples.en: This bus goes to the airport via City Hall.
I flew from Incheon to New York by way of Tokyo.

examples.ko: 홍콩을 경유하는 비행기 표가 더 싸요.
examples.en: The flight ticket with a stopover in Hong Kong is cheaper.

examples.ko: 부산에 갈 때 대전을 경유할 거예요.
examples.en: I will go through Daejeon on my way to Busan.
Where did you stop over on the way back?

examples.ko: 이 길은 시장을 경유하고 학교로 이어져요.
examples.en: This road passes through the market and leads to the school.

explain: 버스나 비행기 안내에서 많이 써요. 말할 때는 '거쳐서 가다'가 더 자연스러워요. 거치는 곳 앞에는 '을/를'을 붙이고, '경유'는 자동차 연료 이름이기도 해요.

phrases.en: There is a bus that goes via the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경유하는'으로 바꿔서 버스나 비행기를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form '경유하는' describes a bus or flight.

phrases.en: I will go to Busan via Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '경유하다' 대신 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural spoken alternative to '경유하다'.

phrases.en: Where is the stopover?
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기나 버스가 중간에 들르는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the place where a flight or bus stops on the way.

explain_en: You hear it a lot in bus and flight announcements. In casual speech '거쳐서 가다' sounds more natural. The place you pass through takes '을/를', and '경유' is also the word for diesel fuel.

examples.ko: 뒤 차가 계속 경적을 울려서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The car behind kept honking, which startled me.
The baby woke up and cried at the sound of the horn.

examples.ko: 밤에는 경적을 함부로 울리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not honk carelessly at night.
As soon as the light changed, horns went off all around.

examples.ko: 저는 급한 일이 아니면 경적을 거의 안 눌러요.
examples.en: Unless it's urgent, I almost never press the horn.
The train passed by with a long blast of its horn.

explain: '경적'은 자동차, 기차, 배가 주변에 알리려고 내는 큰 소리나 장치예요. 보통 '경적을 울리다'로 말하고 '빵빵거리다'는 더 편한 말이에요. 한국에서는 불필요한 경적이 시끄럽다고 느껴서 조심하는 편이에요.

phrases.en: A horn suddenly sounded loudly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 나는 쪽을 주어로 하여 일어난 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes the horn the subject to describe what happened.

phrases.en: The driver keeps honking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경적을 울리다'보다 편한 말로, 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual way to say 경적을 울리다, common in daily talk.

phrases.en: Please don't honk your horn in front of the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용히 해야 하는 곳에서 부탁하는 말로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request used in places that need to be quiet.

explain_en: 경적 is the loud signal or device a car, train, or ship uses to warn others. The usual phrase is 경적을 울리다, and 빵빵거리다 is a more casual way to say it. In Korea, unnecessary honking is seen as noisy, so drivers tend to be careful.

examples.en: There's a construction site next to my house, so it's noisy every morning.

examples.ko: 옆에선 새로 주택을 짓느라 공사판이 한창이었어요.
examples.en: Next door, the construction site was in full swing building new houses.
I worked a part-time job at a construction site during vacation.
The road is dug up like a construction site, so it's hard to walk.
You must wear a hard hat at a construction site.

examples.ko: 아빠가 젊을 때 공사판을 돌아다니며 일하셨대요.
examples.en: They say my dad went around working at construction sites when he was young.

explain: '공사장'이 중립적인 말이고, '공사판'은 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 말이라 일하는 사람들의 일터 느낌이 있어요. 격식 있는 글이나 안내문에서는 '공사장'이나 '공사 현장'이 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: It's dangerous in front of the construction site, so be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공사판'보다 중립적이고 안내문에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More neutral than 공사판 and usable on signs and notices.

phrases.en: You must wear a helmet at a construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 격식 있는 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used in formal writing and the news.

phrases.en: My father worked at construction sites when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일터라는 느낌이 있어서 일하는 이야기를 할 때 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: It has a workplace feel, so it is natural when talking about work.
phrases.en_equiv: to work at a construction site

explain_en: '공사장' is the neutral word, while '공사판' is a casual spoken word with the feel of a workplace for laborers. In formal writing or notices, '공사장' or '공사 현장' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The drought was severe, so a water truck came to the village.

examples.ko: 급수차 앞에 주민들이 물통을 들고 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: Residents lined up with water containers in front of the water truck.
I got water from the water truck and washed the kids.
The fire station agreed to send a water truck.

examples.ko: 급수차는 하루에 두 번 오는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The water truck seems to come twice a day.
Boil the water you get from the water truck before drinking.

explain: 가뭄이나 단수, 공사로 수돗물이 안 나올 때 물을 실어 와 나눠 주는 차예요. 뉴스에서 재난이나 단수 이야기가 나올 때 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: When the water was cut off, a water truck came in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 안 나오는 곳에 급수차가 도착했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a water truck arrives where water has stopped running.

phrases.en: Residents took water from the water truck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 급수차 옆에서 물을 가져가는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes people collecting water at the truck.
phrases.en_equiv: to get water from the truck

phrases.en: City Hall sent a water truck to the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 필요한 곳으로 차를 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a truck is sent to a place that needs water.

explain_en: It is a truck that brings and distributes water when tap water is unavailable because of drought, outages or construction. You often hear it in news about disasters or water cuts.

examples.ko: 지진이 나면 가까운 대피소로 가야 해요.
examples.en: If an earthquake happens, you must go to the nearest shelter.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 대피소 위치를 확인해 봤어요.
examples.en: I checked where the shelter in our neighborhood is.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 주민들이 대피소에서 하룻밤을 보냈어요.
examples.en: The residents spent a night at the shelter because of the typhoon.
Water and blankets were prepared at the shelter.
I heard that this subway station is used as a shelter.

examples.ko: 아이들이 놀라지 않게 대피소까지 손을 잡고 갔어요.
examples.en: We held hands all the way to the shelter so the children wouldn't be scared.

explain: '대피소'는 재난이 났을 때 잠깐 몸을 피하는 곳이에요. 오래 지내는 '임시 주거지'와는 달라요. 안내 방송에서는 '대피소로 이동하세요'처럼 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I heard the announcement and moved to the shelter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난 안내 방송에서 자주 듣는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often heard in disaster announcements.

phrases.en: The school gym became a temporary shelter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠깐 몸을 피하려고 정한 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A place set up for a short stay to get out of danger.

phrases.en: There was a fire, so everyone evacuated outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대피소에 가는 동작을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for the act of going to safety, as in a shelter.

explain_en: A 대피소 is a place to take cover briefly when a disaster strikes, different from longer-term temporary housing. In emergency announcements you often hear 대피소로 이동하세요. It is the destination you head to right away.

en: to be packed with; to be full of

examples.en: The subway is jam-packed during rush hour.
The amusement park was bursting with people on the weekend.
I packed the bag so full it could burst.
The store is packed on the first day of the sale.
The bus was so packed that I let one go.

examples.ko: 미어터지는 식당 앞에서 한 시간을 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I waited an hour in front of the jam-packed restaurant.

explain: 사람이나 물건이 너무 많아서 터질 것 같을 때 쓰는 구어체 표현이에요. '붐비다'보다 훨씬 강하고 생생한 느낌이라 친구와 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: Every morning I commute on a packed subway.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며요. 사람이 아주 많은 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는' lets it describe a noun that is extremely crowded.

phrases.en: At lunchtime the restaurant looks like it will be packed to bursting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 사람이 너무 많아질 것 같다는 예상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to predict that a place is about to become overcrowded.
phrases.en_equiv: looks like it will burst with people

phrases.en: On weekday afternoons the bus isn't packed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 많지 않고 여유가 있다는 뜻으로, 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says a place is not crowded.

explain_en: It is a colloquial word for when there are so many people or things that it feels ready to burst. It is much stronger and more vivid than '붐비다', so it fits chats with friends.

examples.en: The police put up a barricade on the road.

examples.ko: 공사 구간 앞에 바리케이드가 세워져 있어요.
examples.en: A barricade has been set up in front of the construction section.

examples.ko: 바리케이드 때문에 차가 지나갈 수 없었어요.
examples.en: Cars couldn't get through because of the barricade.
They installed barricades on both sides of the road.
People are waiting in front of the barricade.
On festival days they block the street with barricades.

explain: 길이나 입구를 막아 놓은 구조물이에요. 공사, 행사, 사고 현장에서 볼 수 있고 '바리케이드를 치다, 설치하다'처럼 말해요. '바리게이트'라고 쓰는 사람도 있지만 표준 표기는 '바리케이드'예요.

phrases.en: They put up a barricade at the entrance to the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 막기 위해 설치한다는 뜻으로 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say setting up a barrier to block a road.

phrases.en: They set up barricades on the road because of the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치다'보다 조금 더 공식적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A little more formal than '치다'.

phrases.en: They blocked off the accident site with barricades.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳을 바리케이드로 막을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when blocking off a place with barricades.

explain_en: It is a structure set up to block a road or entrance, seen at construction sites, events and accident scenes. People say '바리케이드를 치다' or '설치하다'. Some write '바리게이트', but the standard spelling is '바리케이드'.

en: being in all directions; being all over the place; everywhere

examples.en: The rumor quickly spread in every direction.
I ran around everywhere to find my lost wallet.
The sound of firecrackers comes from all around.
I looked everywhere, but the key isn't there.

examples.ko: 길이 사방팔방으로 뚫려 있어서 어디든 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Roads run in every direction, so you can get anywhere.
Ads are plastered all over the place.

explain: '여기저기'와 비슷하지만 모든 방향이라는 과장된 느낌이 더 강해요. 소문이 퍼지거나, 뭔가를 찾아 헤매거나, 소리가 사방에서 들릴 때 자주 써요. 보통 '사방팔방으로', '사방팔방에서', '사방팔방 뛰어다니다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: When the balloon burst, the pieces scattered in every direction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가가 모든 방향으로 퍼질 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something spreads out in every direction.

phrases.en: I can hear cheering from every direction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리나 사람이 여러 곳에서 올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sounds or people come from many places.

phrases.en: I searched everywhere for my keys.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여기저기'보다 더 크게 과장해서 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sounds more exaggerated than 여기저기.

explain_en: It is similar to '여기저기' but has a stronger, exaggerated feel of every direction. It is often used for spreading rumors, searching all over, or sound coming from all sides. Typical forms are '사방팔방으로', '사방팔방에서' and '사방팔방 뛰어다니다'.

examples.ko: 서울로 가는 상행선은 이쪽 승강장에서 타요.
examples.en: The northbound line to Seoul leaves from this platform.

examples.ko: 사고 때문에 상행선이 한 시간 넘게 막혔어요.
examples.en: The up lane was blocked for over an hour because of an accident.

examples.ko: 상행선 표를 사려면 몇 번 창구로 가야 해요?
examples.en: Which window do I go to for a ticket on the up line?
I have to transfer to the up line but I got lost.
When you get off at the up-line platform, you'll see the exit right away.

examples.ko: 하행선보다 상행선을 타는 사람이 더 많아요.
examples.en: More people take the up line than the down line.

explain: 기차나 고속도로에서 보통 서울 쪽으로 향하는 방향을 말하고, 반대 방향은 '하행선'이에요. 주말 저녁에 고속도로 정체를 알릴 때 '상행선이 막힌다'라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The down line to Busan is at that platform over there.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상행선'의 반대말로, 서울에서 멀어지는 방향이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '상행선': the direction away from Seoul.

phrases.en: The up-line train is arriving soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서울 쪽으로 가는 기차를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for trains heading toward Seoul.

phrases.en: The inbound lanes get very jammed on Sunday evenings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주말 고속도로 교통 상황을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for weekend highway traffic reports.

explain_en: On trains and expressways it usually means the direction heading toward Seoul, and the opposite direction is '하행선'. You often hear '상행선이 막힌다' in weekend-evening traffic reports.

examples.en: It is dangerous if people go onto the tracks.

examples.ko: 선로 공사 때문에 기차가 늦게 와요.
examples.en: The train comes late because of track work.
A cat was walking along the tracks.

examples.ko: 지하철 선로에 물건을 떨어뜨리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not drop things onto the subway tracks.
The tracks were flooded by the heavy rain.
A staff member is inspecting the tracks.

explain: '선로'는 기차나 지하철이 다니는 철로 전체를 말해요. 뉴스와 안내방송에서 '선로 점검', '선로 안전'처럼 자주 들리고, 일상에서는 '철길'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Staff check the tracks every night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기차가 안전한지 선로를 확인하는 일이에요. 안내방송에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Checking the tracks to make sure trains are safe. Often heard in announcements.

phrases.example: 선로 위에 물건을 놓으면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You must not put things on the tracks.
phrases.nuance_ko: '위'를 붙여서 선로 위쪽에 있다는 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 위 (on top of) says where something is in relation to the tracks.

phrases.en: There is a small village next to the railroad.
phrases.nuance_ko: '선로'보다 일상적인 말이에요. 기찻길이라는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 선로, with the feel of a train path.

explain_en: 선로 means the railway tracks that trains and subways run on. You hear it in the news and announcements as '선로 점검' or '선로 안전', and in daily speech people also say 철길.

examples.en: The police found the criminal gang's hideout.
I heard that building was a den of thieves.

examples.ko: 영화 속 악당은 산속 소굴에 숨어 있었어요.
examples.en: The villain in the movie was hiding in a lair in the mountains.

examples.ko: 우리 방은 완전히 쓰레기 소굴이 됐어요.
examples.en: Our room has turned into a complete pigsty.

examples.ko: 아이들이 놀고 나면 거실이 장난감 소굴처럼 변해요.
examples.en: After the kids play, the living room turns into a toy den.

examples.ko: 친구 집에 갔더니 게임 소굴로 변해 있었어요.
examples.en: When I went to my friend's house, it had turned into a gaming den.

explain: 나쁜 사람이나 범죄 무리가 모여 사는 본거지를 말하고, 비유로 지저분하거나 어수선한 곳에도 써요. '아지트'는 친구들끼리의 비밀 장소처럼 좋은 느낌으로도 쓰지만 '소굴'은 늘 부정적이에요.

phrases.en: That empty house was a den of thieves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 무리가 모인 곳에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a place where bad people gather.

phrases.example: 그 골목은 범죄의 소굴로 알려져 있어요.
phrases.en: That alley is known as a den of crime.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 글에서 자주 보이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in news and writing.

phrases.en: The abandoned building became a dump.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지저분한 곳을 비유할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used figuratively for a messy place.

explain_en: It means the base where bad people or criminals gather, and figuratively a filthy or chaotic place. '아지트' can feel friendly, like a secret spot for friends, but '소굴' is always negative.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 언덕배기에 있어서 겨울에 오르기 힘들어요.
examples.en: Our house is on a hillside, so it's hard to climb in winter.
The night view from the top of the hill is wonderful.

examples.ko: 언덕배기를 따라 작은 집들이 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Small houses are clustered along the hill slope.
The children are flying kites on the hill.
I rode my bike up the steep hill.

examples.ko: 언덕배기 끝에 오래된 나무 한 그루가 서 있어요.
examples.en: At the end of the hill stands one old tree.

explain: '언덕'보다 입말 느낌이 강하고, 언덕의 꼭대기나 비탈진 곳을 정겹게 말할 때 어울려요. 동네 풍경을 이야기할 때 '언덕배기에 있는 집'처럼 많이 써요. 글에서는 '언덕'이 더 무난해요.

phrases.en: I climbed the hilltop, gasping for breath.
phrases.nuance_ko: '를/을'을 붙여 오르는 대상으로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 을/를 it becomes the object being climbed.

phrases.en: It's a neighborhood on a hill, so there are many stairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 언덕 위 마을을 정겹게 부르는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A warm way to call a neighborhood built on a hill.

phrases.en: Children are running around on the hilltop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 어떤 일이 일어나는 장소로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 에서 it marks the place where something happens.

explain_en: It feels more colloquial than '언덕' and fits when you fondly refer to the top or slope of a hill. It is often used in descriptions of a neighborhood, as in '언덕배기에 있는 집'. In writing, '언덕' is the safer choice.

examples.en: The electric train slowly pulls into the station.

examples.ko: 출근 시간에는 전동차 안이 너무 붐벼요.
examples.en: The train is far too crowded during rush hour.
I missed the last train, so I took a taxi.
The new trains have much more comfortable seats.
The train doors are closing, so be careful.
The children watched the trains pass by outside the window.

explain: 일상에서는 보통 '지하철'이나 '전철'이라고 해요. '전동차'는 열차 자체를 가리킬 때나 안내 방송, 뉴스에서 더 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I commute by subway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '전동차'보다 '지하철'이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, '지하철' is much more natural than '전동차'.

phrases.en: Please be quiet inside the train car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내 방송에서 열차 안을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in announcements for the inside of the train.

phrases.en: The train is arriving, so please step back.
phrases.nuance_ko: 역에 열차가 도착할 때 쓰는 안내 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical announcement sentence when a train arrives at the station.

explain_en: In daily speech people usually say 지하철 or 전철. 전동차 refers to the train itself and is heard more often in station announcements and the news.

examples.en: The two teams' opinions clashed head-on in the meeting.
Drive carefully so the cars don't collide head-on.
The two people almost ran straight into each other at the corner.
If each only insists on their own view, they clash head-on.
As the two policies clashed head-on, the debate grew.

examples.ko: 아침에 자전거와 오토바이가 정면충돌한 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: This morning I saw a bicycle and a motorbike collide head-on.

explain: '~와/과 정면충돌하다'로 써서 서로 마주 부딪친다는 뜻이에요. 사고뿐 아니라 의견, 이익, 정책이 크게 맞설 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The two cars collided head-on at the intersection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 일어난 사고를 과거형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for an accident that has already happened.

phrases.en: It's dangerous if cars collide head-on on a narrow road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-면'으로 조건을 말하는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form using -면 for a condition.

phrases.en: The two people's opinions clashed head-on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고뿐 아니라 의견이 크게 맞설 때도 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only for accidents but also when opinions strongly oppose each other.

explain_en: Used as '~와/과 정면충돌하다', meaning to run straight into one another. It covers accidents as well as opinions, interests or policies that strongly oppose each other.

examples.en: A forklift is moving cargo in the warehouse.
You need a license to drive a forklift.
It's dangerous to walk in front of a forklift.
My uncle lifted the boxes high with a forklift.

examples.ko: 지게차는 무거운 물건을 들어 올릴 때 써요.
examples.en: A forklift is used when lifting heavy things.
I was almost run over by a forklift and was startled.

explain: 공장이나 창고, 물류센터에서 쓰는 차예요. '지게차를 운전하다'라고 말하고 자격증이 필요해요. 공사장에서 땅을 파는 차(굴착기)와는 달라요.

phrases.en: My father drives a forklift at the factory.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 몰 때 쓰는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for driving the vehicle.

phrases.en: I want to get a forklift license.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하려면 필요한 자격을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the license needed for the job.

phrases.en: We moved the heavy boxes with a forklift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무거운 짐을 옮기는 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say how heavy loads are moved.

explain_en: It is a vehicle used in factories, warehouses and logistics centers. You say '지게차를 운전하다', and a license is required. It differs from the digging machine (굴착기) at construction sites.

examples.ko: 채석장에서 큰 돌을 잘라 내고 있어요.
examples.en: They are cutting out big stones at the quarry.
The old quarry has now become a park.

examples.ko: 채석장 근처는 먼지가 많아서 마스크를 써야 해요.
examples.en: There's a lot of dust near the quarry, so you need to wear a mask.

examples.ko: 견학 가서 채석장의 거대한 돌벽을 봤어요.
examples.en: On the field trip, I saw the quarry's huge stone walls.

examples.ko: 채석장으로 가는 길은 트럭이 많이 다녀요.
examples.en: Lots of trucks drive on the road to the quarry.

examples.ko: 채석장에 가 보면 돌 색깔이 정말 다양해요.
examples.en: If you go to a quarry, the colors of the stone are really varied.

explain: 건물이나 길을 만들 돌을 캐내는 곳이에요. 석탄이나 철 같은 광물을 캐는 곳은 '광산'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 지금은 쓰지 않는 채석장이 공원이나 관광지로 바뀐 곳도 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 건물은 근처 채석장에서 나온 돌로 지었어요.
phrases.en: This building was built with stone from a nearby quarry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건축 재료의 출처를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say where building material came from.

phrases.en: People dig stone out of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 채석장에서 하는 일을 쉽게 설명하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to describe the work done at a quarry.

phrases.en: The old quarry site has now become a lake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 채석장이던 자리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the place where a quarry used to be.

explain_en: It is a place where stone for buildings and roads is dug out. A place that mines minerals like coal or iron is a '광산', which is different. Some disused quarries have been turned into parks or tourist spots.

examples.en: The train crosses the iron bridge slowly.
A train passes over the Han River railway bridge.

examples.ko: 오래된 철교가 낡아서 새로 놓기로 했어요.
examples.en: The old iron bridge is worn out, so they decided to build a new one.
Many people fish under the iron bridge.

examples.ko: 철교를 건널 때 창밖 경치가 멋있었어요.
examples.en: The view out the window was beautiful as we crossed the bridge.
It's dangerous to take photos on a railway bridge.

explain: 쇠로 만든 다리이고, 실제로는 기차나 지하철이 다니는 다리를 가리킬 때가 많아요. 자동차가 다니는 일반 다리는 보통 그냥 '다리'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The river looks beautiful from the iron bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다리 위쪽 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Indicates the top of the bridge.

phrases.en: When the subway crosses the iron bridge, you can see the Han River.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기차나 지하철이 다리를 통과할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for trains or subways passing over the bridge.

phrases.example: 강 위에 낡은 철교가 하나 있어요.
phrases.en: There is an old iron bridge over the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래된 쇠다리의 모습을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an aged iron bridge.

explain_en: It is a bridge made of iron, and in practice it often refers to a bridge that trains or subways run over. An ordinary bridge for cars is usually just called '다리'.
